sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Henry County, Missouri?
sections.html:
Two offices share the courthouse address, 100 West Franklin in Clinton, MO 64735. The Assessor sets values: the county's page lists Scott Largent, phone 660-885-7212, open weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with weekends and evenings by appointment. The Treasurer, who also serves as Ex Officio Collector of Revenue, sends and collects the bills at 660-885-7207, according to the State Tax Commission's collector directory.

The directory also lists a fax at 660-885-7259 and the email collector@henrycountymo.net. Use the assessor for questions about value and the collector for questions about what you owe.

sections.h2: What is Henry County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Henry County lies in western Missouri and was organized in December 1834 as Rives County, then renamed for Patrick Henry in 1841. Clinton is the seat, and the county's own site puts it at roughly 8,945 residents, ahead of Windsor at 2,847. Smaller towns include Calhoun, Deepwater, Montrose, Urich, Blairstown, Brownington and Tightwad.

Land area is 697 square miles. The county site says agriculture is the economic base and that most of the hilly, wooded ground sits near the 55,600 acre Harry S. Truman Reservoir, which draws anglers and hunters. Routes 7, 13, 18 and 52 cross the county. About 59.6 percent of residents lived in rural areas at the 2020 census.

School districts named for county communities include Clinton, Windsor (Henry County R-1), Calhoun R-VIII, Montrose R-XIV, Davis R-XII, Leesville R-IX and Shawnee R-III.

sections.h2: Where does Henry County sit, and how old is the county seat?
sections.html:
Henry County borders Johnson, Pettis, Benton, St. Clair, Bates and Cass counties. The county site traces first settlement to 1830, and says the seat was picked in the fall of 1836 and named Clinton for New York Governor DeWitt Clinton. The county has had two courthouses, and the cornerstone of the present one was laid on June 24, 1892.

The 2020 census counted 21,946 people with a median age of 44.7 years, and 22.9 percent were 65 or older. At that census 70.2 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied.

sections.h2: How is a Henry County house assessed?
sections.html:
Missouri sets residential real property at 19 percent of true value, agricultural land at 12 percent and commercial property at 32 percent, per RSMo 137.115. Values are reset on January 1 of odd-numbered years and carry into the next even year, except that new construction and improvements are valued as though finished on that earlier odd-year date.

  • If the assessor raises a residential value by more than 15 percent since the last assessment, not counting new construction, a physical inspection is required.
  • The owner gets written notice of that right and at least 30 days to ask for an interior inspection.
  • A drive-by does not count as an inspection under the statute.

On appeal, RSMo 138.060 says the assessor's value carries no presumption of being correct, and in any county the assessor must prove the value does not exceed market value when it rose at least 15 percent without new construction.

sections.h2: What dates matter on a Henry County tax calendar?
sections.html:
Missouri ties property tax to the first day of the year, so the owner on January 1 is the one assessed. The dates that matter to a Henry County owner or seller:

  • January 1: assessment date for real and personal property
  • Odd-numbered years: new real estate values are set
  • Second Monday in July: last day to file with the Board of Equalization
  • December 31: bills are due and mailed payments must be postmarked
  • January 1 after that: the collector adds a penalty to unpaid tax
  • Fourth Monday in August: delinquent land can be sold

A house sold in spring still has that year's bill coming in November, so ask your title company how the closing statement splits it.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Henry County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the county Board of Equalization. The State Tax Commission's guidance puts the deadline at the second Monday in July, and the Board must decide before the next step. If you disagree with the Board, you have 30 days from the date of its decision letter to complain to the State Tax Commission, which accepts filings online, by email at Legal@stc.mo.gov or by mail to PO Box 146, Jefferson City, MO 65102-0146.

If a corporation, LLC, limited partnership, trust or estate owns the property, an attorney must file the State Tax Commission appeal. Attach a copy of the tax bill or the Board's decision letter. If you signed a stipulated value with the assessor, that settles the matter and ends the right to appeal further.

Ask the Henry County Assessor for this year's local filing steps and form.

sections.h2: When are Henry County property taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
sections.html:
Missouri bills are due by December 31, and mailed payments count as on time by postmark date under RSMo 139.100. After January 1 the collector adds a penalty to what remains unpaid. Ask the Henry County collector for the exact bill date and penalty amount.

Paying under protest is an option when you dispute a value. Under RSMo 139.031 you pay the full bill before the delinquency date, file a written statement of your grounds with the collector, and start a circuit court action within ninety days. The State Tax Commission adds that you may appeal to the Board of Equalization or the Commission even if you have not yet paid.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Henry County house that has unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Delinquent tax stays attached to the land until it is cleared. Under RSMo 140.150, land with delinquent taxes is subject to sale on the fourth Monday of August, and you can still pay the delinquent tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector any time before the sale. The collector must mail notice to the recorded owner first, and not receiving it does not cancel the debt.

Before you list, ask the collector at 660-885-7207 for a payoff figure on your parcel, and give the number to your title company so it can be paid from closing proceeds. Ask the assessor at 660-885-7212 whether any exemption or credit applies to your situation.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Henry County?
faqs.a: The Henry County Treasurer, who is also the Ex Officio Collector of Revenue, handles bills and payments. The office is at 100 West Franklin in Clinton, and the state directory lists 660-885-7207.

faqs.q: What percent of value does Henry County tax on a house?
faqs.a: Missouri assesses residential property at 19 percent of true value. Farmland is 12 percent and commercial property is 32 percent. Your tax bill then applies the local levy rates to that assessed value.

faqs.q: When is the last day to pay property tax in Henry County?
faqs.a: December 31. A mailed payment counts as timely if the postmark is on or before that date. After January 1 the collector adds a penalty to unpaid taxes.

faqs.q: Can Henry County sell my house for back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Missouri law makes land with unpaid taxes subject to sale on the fourth Monday of August. You can pay the tax, penalty, interest and costs to the collector before the sale to stop it.

faqs.q: Where do I ask the Henry County Assessor about my value?
faqs.a: Call 660-885-7212 or visit 100 West Franklin in Clinton. The office is open weekdays from 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and the county site says weekends and evenings are possible by appointment.
